title: the client reads the port of a service that is gone: the reader of the file of the port answers nil and does not die on the filesystem
intent: The wave repairs the third of the three places that the survey of the class of the defect named on 2026-11-21.  The service publishes the number of its port in a file next to its socket (`lib/yeah-service.el:105-108`) and removes that file when it stops (`lib/yeah-service.el:228-230`), so the file of the port is gone by the time the client reads it -- and it can be gone between the moment the reader looks for it and the moment it reads it.  The reader of the file of the port (`lib/yeah-client.el:59-69`) asked the file whether it can be read and read it afterwards, so the read died with `file-missing' when the file vanished in between, and the death left the reader and with it the client: the client of the editor fell on the filesystem where its docstring promised to wait for a service that is not there yet.  The error of the file was not caught at all, and the `condition-case' of the caller (`lib/yeah-client.el:86-99`) covers the `make-network-process' and not the reading of the port, so the failure left the client as well.  The repair is that the reader of the port decides: it catches the error of the file and nothing else and answers nil, and nil is what the docstring promises and what the caller waits for.  The four kinds of the absence of the port are all `file-error' (measured on Emacs 30.2: `file-missing' and `permission-denied' are its kinds, and the reading of a directory gives `file-error' as well), so one handler covers them and no handler of `error' is needed.  The proof of the repair is a new check of 295 lines with eleven stands, among them the stand that reads the file of the port of a service that stops while the client reads it -- the vanishing is made by the check and not waited for -- and the stand that proves that the reader hides the error of the file and nothing else: an error that is not an error of the file is raised and not swallowed.  The claim of the wave is new.
objection: The wave repairs a reader and not a feature, and the price is named.  (a) **The repair does not hide the failure of the read**: only the error of the file is caught, and the stand 8 of the check proves that an error that is not an error of the file is raised and not swallowed -- a reader that swallowed every error would decide nothing, and a check that cannot tell the two apart is a check that proves nothing.  (b) **The repair does not promise more than it can keep**: the client still waits for a service that is not there and still says that there is no service on it (the stands 9 and 10), and the promise of the docstring -- nil where the port is unavailable -- is kept.  (c) **The repair did not weaken the reader**: a file of the port that holds a port is read as that port (the stand 7), and a file that holds text and not a port, or a port out of range, is nil (the stands 5 and 6) -- the reader that answers nil for everything would pass the repair and would be a reader that decides nothing.  (d) **The pre-check stayed, and that is named**: `file-readable-p' is still asked first, because the client polls the file every 50 ms while it waits for a service, and the promise of the check is not used any more -- the reading is under the `condition-case', so the check of the repair does not depend on which of the two forms of the repair was written.  (e) **The class of the defect is not closed**: this wave closes the third of the three places that the survey of 2026-11-21 named; the survey counted 42 places of the class and named 19 of them dangerous, and the rest of them are named in the wave 100 and in the wave 101.  (f) **One run of `check-service-tcp.el' failed for a reason that is not the repair**: the host was under a load of 21 on four CPUs (other sessions were building OCaml and running `bun test' and `pytest'), and the client did not connect within its ten seconds; the same check passes on the new tree and on the old tree seven times out of eight, and the same pair was run again on the new tree and passed.  It is named here because a failure that is not measured is a failure that is not known.
refuted_by: the reader of the port raises an error where the port is unavailable, or the reader answers a port for a file that holds text and not a port, or the reader answers a port that is out of range, or the reader answers nil for a port that is published, or the reader hides an error that is not an error of the file, or the client dies on the file where it promised to wait, or the client does not wait for a service that is not there, or the stop of a service leaves the file of the port behind, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The wave is one of the three that close the class of the defect that the survey of 2026-11-21 found, and it is the last of the three.  (1) **The defect was a promise that was not kept**: the docstring of the reader of the port promised nil where the port is unavailable, and the reader raised an error where the port was unavailable -- the file of the port is deleted by the stop of the service, and the client read it in the middle of that stop.  (2) **The repair is in one place and it is small**: the reader of the file of the port catches the error of the file and nothing else and answers nil; the caller was not touched, the wire was not touched, and no surface of the interface was touched.  (3) **The proof holds eleven stands and can fail by each of them**; the bite of the control of the claim was measured by the writer on a copy of the tree (the mutation of the handler of the reader, addressed with `0,/…/' because the file holds two handlers of the same name), and by the parent on a copy of the tree (2026-11-21): three controls, 0 failures -- the honest tree passes (C103a), the old code does not pass and refuses with three of its own assertions (C103b), and the reader that hides the failure of the read does not pass and refuses with three named assertions (C103c).  (4) **The first mutation of the parent bit for the wrong reason and was corrected**: the mutation was one closing parenthesis short, the file did not parse, and the check failed with a parse error and not by its own assertion -- a false refusal with a false subject is worse than no refusal at all; the mutation was balanced and run again, and the registered control is the one that refuses by its own assertions.  (5) **The claim of the wave is new** (`the-client-reads-the-port-of-a-service-that-is-gone') and it amends no claim of the package; the scope of the claim is the reader and its check, and `lib/yeah-service.el' is not in the scope: it was not changed, and the check uses it as the source of the real removal of the file.
